text: It depends what I'm shopping for. I quite like browsing in bookshops or markets, because there's no pressure and you often find something unexpected. But shopping for clothes in a crowded mall is a different story — I usually get tired after about half an hour.

tips.en: Two kinds of shopping with reasons — more than a yes or no.
tips.kk: Екі түрлі сауда себептерімен — жауап «иә» не «жоқпен» шектелмейді.
tips.ru: Два вида покупок с причинами — ответ не сводится к «да» или «нет».
tips.example: It depends what I'm shopping for

tips.en: A different story is a natural way to contrast.
tips.kk: A different story — қарама-қарсы қоюдың табиғи тәсілі.
tips.ru: A different story — естественный способ противопоставить.

note.en: Looking at things without planning to buy.

text: For everyday things I mostly shop online now, since it saves time and prices are often lower. That said, I still prefer going to a shop for clothes and shoes, because I need to try them on — I've ordered the wrong size online far too many times.

tips.en: Different answers for different purchases — precise and mature.
tips.kk: Әртүрлі сатып алуға әртүрлі жауап — парасатты, дәл жауап.
tips.ru: Разные ответы для разных покупок — зрелый, точный ответ.
tips.example: For everyday things I mostly shop online now

tips.en: A short real story makes the reason convincing.
tips.kk: Өмірден алынған қысқа оқиға дәлелді сенімді етеді.
tips.ru: Короткая история из жизни делает довод убедительным.
tips.example: I've ordered the wrong size online far too many times

note.en: A phrasal verb: put clothes on to check them.

questions.question: Do you prefer shopping online or in shops?

text: There's a small bakery near my flat that I go to almost every morning. The owner remembers what I usually order, and the bread is always fresh. It's a tiny thing, but it makes the start of the day feel a bit more personal than buying coffee at a big chain.

tips.en: Where, how often and why — lively and specific.
tips.kk: Қайда, қаншалықты жиі және неге — жауап тірі әрі нақты.
tips.ru: Где, как часто и почему — ответ живой и конкретный.
tips.example: The owner remembers what I usually order

tips.en: The last sentence explains why it matters.
tips.kk: Соңғы сөйлем мұның неге маңызды екенін түсіндіреді.
tips.ru: Последняя фраза объясняет, почему это важно.

questions.followUp: What do you like about it?
questions.question: Is there a shop you often go to?

text: More often than I'd like to admit. Online sales are my weakness — when something is fifty per cent off, it suddenly feels like a bargain, even if I never planned to buy it. I've started waiting a day before paying, and usually I realise I don't want it after all.

tips.en: An honest admission sounds natural and friendly.
tips.kk: Шынайы мойындау табиғи естіліп, жылы әсер қалдырады.
tips.ru: Честное признание звучит естественно и располагает.
tips.example: More often than I'd like to admit

tips.en: The answer ends with what the speaker does about it.
tips.kk: Жауап автордың мұнымен не істейтінімен аяқталады.
tips.ru: Ответ заканчивается тем, что автор с этим делает.
tips.example: I've started waiting a day before paying

note.en: “In the end, despite what I thought”.

questions.question: Do you ever buy things you do not really need?

text: Enormously. A few years ago people went to bazaars and shopping centres at weekends, but now almost everything can be ordered on an app and delivered within hours. It's incredibly convenient, although I think small local shops are finding it much harder to survive.

tips.en: Comparing past and present is a natural structure for a question about change.
tips.kk: Өткен мен қазірді салыстыру — өзгеріс туралы сұраққа табиғи құрылым.
tips.ru: Сравнение прошлого и настоящего — естественная структура для вопроса о переменах.
tips.example: A few years ago people went to bazaars and shopping centres

tips.en: Although shows both the benefit and the cost of the change.
tips.kk: Although өзгерістің жақсы да, жаман да жағын көрсетеді.
tips.ru: Although показывает и плюс, и минус перемен.
tips.example: although I think small local shops are finding it much harder

questions.question: Has the way people shop changed in recent years?
